q: "找出年龄在 20-25 之间的用户"为什么在数据库里毫秒级返回?
q_en: Why can a database answer "find users aged 20 to 25" in milliseconds?
scenario: 1 亿行用户表,age 上有 B-tree 索引,冷缓存下第一次查 20-25 岁仍是毫秒返回。
scenario_en: You have a 100-million-row users table with a B-tree on age, and even on a cold cache the very first 20-to-25 range query comes back in milliseconds.
options: 年龄这一列取值范围小,所以扫描起来更快
B-tree 把排序键打包同页,一次寻道加顺序读
这条查询结果恰好被数据库缓存住了
年龄是整数类型,整数比较比字符串快,所以范围查询才这么快
why: B-tree 里 20 挨着 21 挨着 22,同页存放,范围查询变成一次寻道加短顺序读——这是现代数据库最擅长的事。
why_en: A B-tree packs sorted keys together on disk, so a range query becomes one seek plus a short sequential read.
options_en: The age column just doesn't have much data.
A B-tree packs sorted keys onto the same page, so a range query is one seek plus a sequential read.
The database happened to cache this query's result.
Age is an integer type, and integer comparisons beat string ones, so the range query is this fast.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种把排序键打包进磁盘页、天然保持平衡的树形索引结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree is a self-balancing tree index that packs sorted keys into disk pages for fast range scans.

optionExplanations: 把速度归因于年龄取值少,但决定范围查询快慢的是索引页里的排序局部性,不是基数高低。
本质是索引页里排序键紧挨着存放,查一个区间只需跳一次再顺着往下读,不必逐行扫表。
缓存能加速重复查询,但冷缓存或换一个新区间照样很快,说明真正原因不是缓存命中。
整数比较确实便宜,可真正贵的是磁盘寻道,没有索引时类型再快也救不了大范围扫描。
optionExplanations_en: This blames the speed on age having few distinct values, but it's really sorted locality inside index pages that matters.
Sorted keys sit packed together on the same page, so a range query just seeks once and reads sequentially from there.
Caching would help repeat queries, but a cold cache or a brand-new range is just as fast, so caching isn't the real reason.
Integer comparisons are cheap, but disk seeks are the expensive part — type alone can't save an unindexed scan.

q: 在 latitude(纬度)一列上建 B-tree 索引,再查"2 公里内的司机",会取回什么?
q_en: If you index only latitude with a B-tree and search for drivers within 2 km, what does it return?
scenario: 网约车派单要找乘客 2 公里内的司机,司机表 1000 万行,只在 latitude 上建了 B-tree 索引。
scenario_en: Dispatch needs drivers within two kilometers of a rider, the driver table has ten million rows, and the only index is a B-tree on latitude.
options: 只返回真正 2 公里内的司机
返回一个以查询点为圆心、2 公里为半径的圆
一条横贯地球的水平条带,经度可能差很远
返回空结果,因为找不到匹配的行
why: 单列索引只按一个维度排序:纬度索引给你一条水平条带,经度索引给你一条垂直条带,都包含海量与你毫无关系的点。
why_en: Indexing latitude alone returns a horizontal strip of the earth, full of points that share latitude but can be thousands of kilometers away.
options_en: It returns exactly the drivers within 2 kilometers.
It returns a circle centered on the query point with a 2-kilometer radius.
A horizontal strip across the globe — similar latitude, but longitude can be worlds apart.
It returns an empty result because nothing matches.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种把排序键打包进磁盘页、天然保持平衡的树形索引结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree is a self-balancing tree index that packs sorted keys into disk pages for fast range scans.

optionExplanations: 这假设单列索引能直接算距离,但纬度索引只按一个维度排序,压根不知道经度差多远。
圆形结果需要同时约束经纬度两个维度,单靠纬度索引连经度信息都没用上,画不出圆。
纬度索引只按纬度排序,取回的是同纬度的一整条横带,里面混着经度差几千公里的点。
只要纬度落在范围内就会命中大量行,不会是空结果,反而会取回一大批无关的点。
optionExplanations_en: This assumes a single-column index can compute distance, but a latitude index only sorts by latitude and knows nothing about longitude.
A circle needs both latitude and longitude constraints; an index on latitude alone never touches longitude at all.
A latitude-only index returns a horizontal band of matching latitude — full of points whose longitude can be worlds apart.
Plenty of rows share that latitude range, so you get a flood of loosely related points, not an empty result.

q: 在 (lat, long) 上建复合索引为什么还是救不了邻近查询?
q_en: Why does a composite index on (lat, long) still fail to solve proximity search?
scenario: 同一张千万行司机表改建 (lat, long) 复合索引,仍要求 2 公里召回在 50 毫秒内返回。
scenario_en: On that same ten-million-row driver table you switch to a composite index on latitude and longitude, and you still need the two-kilometer lookup back in fifty milliseconds.
options: 复合索引没法同时存放两个数字类型的列
仍按第一列一维排序,条带还要逐行暴力算距离
复合索引只支持等值查询,压根不支持范围查询
建立复合索引会导致写入操作被整表锁住
why: 复合索引本质还是先按第一列的一维排序,无法同时压缩两个维度;数据库最终退化为对条带内每行算距离再丢弃 2km 外的暴力扫描。
why_en: A composite index still sorts by the first column and breaks ties with the second, so the database falls back to brute-force distance checks row by row.
options_en: A composite index can't hold two numeric columns at once.
It's still sorted one-dimensionally by the first column, so the strip still needs a row-by-row brute-force distance check.
A composite index only supports equality lookups, not ranges.
Building a composite index locks the whole table.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在多个列上联合建的索引,但排序仍以第一列为主、第二列只用来打破并列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A composite index spans multiple columns, but it still sorts primarily by the first column and only uses the rest to break ties.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种把排序键打包进磁盘页、天然保持平衡的树形索引结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree is a self-balancing tree index that packs sorted keys into disk pages for fast range scans.

optionExplanations: 复合索引完全能存多个列,问题不在存不存得下,而在排序方式没法同时压缩两个维度。
复合索引仍先按第一列排好序,第二列只管打破并列,拉回的条带里还得逐行算距离才能筛干净。
复合索引一样支持范围查询,真正的短板是它只能沿第一列做范围,第二列排序帮不上忙。
建索引确实要付出写入和存储代价,但不会锁死整张表,这不是它解决不了邻近查询的原因。
optionExplanations_en: A composite index can hold multiple columns fine; the problem is its sort order can't compress two dimensions at once.
It still sorts primarily by the first column, using the second only to break ties, so the strip still needs row-by-row checks.
Composite indexes do support range queries — just only efficiently along the first column, not the second.
Building an index costs write and storage overhead, but it doesn't lock the whole table — that's not the real issue here.

q: 补全邻近搜索的根本问题:
q_en: Complete the root problem in proximity search:
text: 根本问题是{{一维}}的排序顺序无法保留{{二维}}的邻近性——把地图压平到一条排序轴上,地面上相邻的点可能在索引里离得{{很远}}。
why: 所有空间索引方案都是在回答同一个问题:如何在一维索引里恢复足够多的二维邻近性,让索引重新有用。
why_en: A one-dimensional sort order cannot preserve two-dimensional closeness, so neighbors on the ground can land far apart in the index.

q: 生产系统解决邻近搜索基本走哪两条路线?
q_en: What are the two main production approaches to proximity search?
scenario: 接手一个 LBS 平台:一半数据是静态的配送区多边形和道路,一半是每秒上报的司机点位。
scenario_en: You inherit a location platform where half the data is static delivery-zone polygons and roads, and half is driver points reporting every second.
options: 内存缓存和磁盘存储:按数据放在哪一层介质分两条路线
SQL 数据库和 NoSQL 数据库
同步复制和异步复制两条路线
空间树(理解形状)和编码键(把位置压成可排序键)
why: 两条路线:几何数据(多边形/道路/配送区)用理解形状的空间树;不断移动的点(司机/用户)用普通索引就能处理的编码键。选哪条取决于数据的形状。
why_en: Production systems either build a custom spatial tree that understands shapes or flatten each location into a single sortable key an ordinary index can handle.
options_en: In-memory caching versus disk storage — splitting by which storage medium the data lives on.
SQL databases versus NoSQL databases.
Synchronous replication versus asynchronous replication.
A spatial tree that understands shapes versus an encoded key that flattens location into a sortable value.

termDefinitions.meaning: Postgres 的空间扩展,基于 GiST 提供 R-tree 式的几何索引能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PostGIS is a Postgres extension that adds R-tree-style spatial indexing on top of GiST.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个搜索引擎,geo 字段底层用 BKD 树索引位置数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Elasticsearch is a search engine whose geo fields are indexed with BKD trees.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把经纬度逐级切成 32 份、拼成一个可排序字符串或整数的位置编码方案。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Geohash recursively divides the world into thirty-two cells per level, encoding a location as a sortable string or integer.

termDefinitions.meaning: Google 提出的球面网格系统,把地球包进立方体六个面再切格子,格子面积全球大致相等。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Google's S2 wraps the globe in a cube and projects onto its six faces, producing roughly equal-area cells anywhere on earth.

termDefinitions.meaning: Uber 开源的六边形网格编码系统,每个格子有 6 个大致等距的邻居,方便环形查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: H3 is Uber's hexagonal grid encoding system, where every cell has six roughly equal-distance neighbors, ideal for ring queries.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的内存型 key-value 存储,自带 geo 系列命令做地理位置索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store with built-in geo commands for location indexing.

optionExplanations: 这把邻近搜索和缓存分层混为一谈,实际两条路线的区分在于数据是形状还是移动点,不是存储介质。
SQL/NoSQL 是存储范式之争,和空间索引要不要理解几何形状是两个完全不同的问题。
复制策略解决的是数据一致性和可用性,跟索引怎么组织空间数据没有关系。
几何数据(多边形/道路)靠理解形状的空间树,移动的点靠能压成可排序键的编码方案,这才是分野。
optionExplanations_en: This conflates proximity search with cache tiering; the real split is shapes versus moving points, not storage medium.
SQL versus NoSQL is a storage-paradigm debate, unrelated to whether a spatial index needs to understand geometry.
Replication strategy is about consistency and availability, not how spatial data gets organized for indexing.
Geometric data like polygons needs a shape-aware spatial tree; moving points just need a sortable encoded key — that's the real split.

q: 贯穿所有空间索引的统一思想是什么?
q_en: What is the common idea behind every spatial index?
scenario: 邻近查询要在 50 毫秒内返回半径 2 公里内的司机,而任何索引的格子都是方的、半径是圆的。
scenario_en: A proximity query must return drivers inside a two-kilometer radius in fifty milliseconds, but every index cell is a square while the radius is a circle.
options: 永远先缩到一小撮候选,再靠精确距离/几何计算收尾
能精确算出最近的 K 个点,不用后续计算
只有全部数据能塞进内存才有效
必须先配合一个机器学习模型预测出热点区域才能工作
why: 每种结构只是"便宜地生成候选集"的不同方式;真正的答案永远由候选集上的精确距离或几何数学算出——永远要后过滤。
why_en: A spatial index never produces the final answer; it cheaply narrows everything down to a small candidate set that exact math then finishes.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A["Earth space"] --> B["Coarse cells"]
  B --> C["Candidate cells"]
  C --> D["Exact distance filter"]
options_en: It always narrows down to a small candidate set first, then finishes with exact distance or geometry math.
It precisely returns the nearest K points with no follow-up math needed.
It only works if the entire dataset fits in memory.
It must be paired with a machine-learning model that predicts hot regions to work.

termDefinitions.meaning: 索引粗筛后留下的一小撮待精确计算的对象,不是最终答案。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A candidate set is the small group of objects an index narrows things down to before exact math finishes the job.

optionExplanations: 每种空间结构做的都是同一件事:先便宜地缩小到一小撮候选,真正的答案永远靠精确计算收尾。
这把索引当成了终点,但没有哪种空间结构能直接给出精确排序结果,后面永远要跟一步精确计算。
磁盘友好的结构(如 BKD、R-tree)正是为了让索引能超出内存工作,并不要求数据全常驻内存。
候选集生成靠的是几何或哈希规则,是确定性算法,不需要引入机器学习模型。
optionExplanations_en: Every spatial structure does the same job: cheaply narrow to a small candidate set, then exact math finishes the real answer.
No spatial structure hands back a precisely ranked final answer by itself — exact math always has to run afterward.
Disk-friendly structures like BKD and R-trees exist precisely so the index can work beyond RAM, not the opposite.
Candidate generation runs on deterministic geometry or hashing rules; it never needs a machine learning model.

scenario: 面试里要为位置功能选索引方案:数据 A 是外卖平台的配送区多边形和道路;数据 B 是每秒都在更新位置的网约车司机点位。
scenario_en: In an interview, you need to choose location indexes: data A is delivery-zone polygons and roads; data B is ride-hailing driver points updated every second.
q: 两类数据分别该走哪条路线?
q_en: Which indexing route fits each data type?
options: A、B 两类数据全部都该用空间树索引
A 用空间树理解形状,B 用编码键换廉价写
A、B 两类数据全都该用编码键
反过来用:A 用编码键,B 却用空间树
why: 口诀:形状用空间树,移动点用编码 cell。几何数据要包含/相交语义,值得付出空间扩展和更贵的写;移动点要的是廉价写和快速候选生成。
why_en: Geometric data with polygons belongs in a spatial tree like PostGIS, while constantly moving points belong in encoded cells on an ordinary index.
whenOtherWins: 如果两类需求混在一个系统里,可以分开索引:形状进 PostGIS、司机位置进编码 cell,各取所长。
options_en: Use a spatial tree for both A and B.
Use a spatial tree for A, since it understands shapes, and an encoded key for B, since writes are cheap.
Use an encoded key for both A and B.
Use an encoded key for A, and — reversed — a spatial tree for B.
tradeoff: 空间树(理解形状,写更贵) vs 编码键(廉价写,只懂点)

termDefinitions.meaning: Postgres 的空间扩展,基于 GiST 提供 R-tree 式的几何索引能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PostGIS is a Postgres extension that adds R-tree-style spatial indexing on top of GiST.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把经纬度逐级切成 32 份、拼成一个可排序字符串或整数的位置编码方案。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Geohash recursively divides the world into thirty-two cells per level, encoding a location as a sortable string or integer.

termDefinitions.meaning: Google 提出的球面网格系统,把地球包进立方体六个面再切格子,格子面积全球大致相等。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Google's S2 wraps the globe in a cube and projects onto its six faces, producing roughly equal-area cells anywhere on earth.

termDefinitions.meaning: Uber 开源的六边形网格编码系统,每个格子有 6 个大致等距的邻居,方便环形查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: H3 is Uber's hexagonal grid encoding system, where every cell has six roughly equal-distance neighbors, ideal for ring queries.

optionExplanations: 配送区多边形确实该用空间树,但司机秒级更新硬套空间树,会被矩形重平衡的写成本拖垮。
多边形要的是包含/相交语义,空间树最懂形状;司机位置只需要廉价写和快速候选,编码键正好够用。
编码键能扛住司机的高频写入,但多边形的包含/相交判断编码键做不了,配送区数据会失真。
反过来用等于两头受苦:配送区丢了几何语义,司机数据又背上了空间树的重写成本。
optionExplanations_en: A spatial tree does fit the delivery polygons, but forcing it onto every-second driver updates means paying rebalancing costs constantly.
Polygons need containment and intersection, which spatial trees understand; driver points just need cheap writes, which encoded keys give you.
Encoded keys handle the driver write volume fine, but they can't answer containment queries, so the polygon data loses meaning.
Swapping them gets the worst of both: polygons lose their geometry, and driver writes inherit expensive tree rebalancing.

q: 让自定义空间树能真正在数据库里(而不只是内存里)工作的关键技巧是什么?
q_en: What trick makes a custom spatial tree work inside a database, not just in memory?
scenario: 要把自研空间树落进按 8KB 页读盘的 PostgreSQL,索引体积远大于机器 RAM。
scenario_en: You want your custom spatial tree to live inside PostgreSQL, which reads disk in eight-kilobyte pages, and the index is far bigger than RAM.
options: 把整棵树完全塞进 RAM 常驻内存里
靠 GPU 做并行加速来加快树的遍历
整形成磁盘 B-tree:页大小节点、深度可控
把整棵树序列化成 JSON 文件存到磁盘上按需读取
why: 数据库按固定页读磁盘;空间树想上盘就得学 B-tree:页大小的平衡节点+可预测深度,否则每个指针都可能是一次随机读。
why_en: Spatial trees work on disk only when shaped like a B-tree, with balanced page-sized nodes and predictable depth.
options_en: Keep the entire tree resident in RAM.
Use a GPU to parallelize tree traversal.
Shape it like an on-disk B-tree: page-sized nodes and predictable depth.
Serialize the whole tree to a JSON file on disk and read it on demand.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种把排序键打包进磁盘页、天然保持平衡的树形索引结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree is a self-balancing tree index that packs sorted keys into disk pages for fast range scans.

optionExplanations: 常驻内存确实能避开磁盘随机读的问题,但数据一旦超过RAM容量就整个不work了,不是通用方案。
GPU 能加速批量计算,但空间树上磁盘的瓶颈是指针跳转造成的随机I/O,并行计算解决不了寻道延迟。
关键是把节点整形成磁盘页大小、深度可预测,这样每次遍历都命中固定大小的页,而不是随机指针跳转。
序列化成JSON能落盘存储,但读取时还是要反序列化重建指针结构,一样避不开随机I/O。
optionExplanations_en: Keeping everything resident in RAM does dodge random disk I/O, but it breaks down the moment data outgrows memory.
A GPU speeds up batch math, but the disk bottleneck here is pointer-chasing random I/O, which parallelism can't shorten.
The trick is shaping nodes to page size with predictable depth, so every traversal hits fixed-size pages instead of random jumps.
Serializing to JSON gets the tree onto disk, but reading it back still means rebuilding pointers — the random I/O problem persists.

q: 四叉树(quadtree)是怎么组织地图的?
q_en: How does a quadtree organize a map?
scenario: 内存里给地图瓦片建索引,点的分布极不均匀:市中心几万个,郊区几乎没有。
scenario_en: You are indexing map tiles in memory and the points are wildly uneven — tens of thousands downtown, almost none in the suburbs.
options: 地图是根,四分象限,超载再分,点住叶子
先按纬度做二分,再按经度做二分
把整张地图切成一批固定大小、互不重叠的网格
为每个数据点建节点,按距离连边
why: quadtree 把地图本身变成树:每个节点四分,超载的象限继续分裂,数据点全部住在叶子里——名字里的"quad"就来自这四路分裂。
why_en: A quadtree makes the map itself the tree, splitting each overloaded quadrant into four children until every leaf holds few points.
diagram:
flowchart TD
    R["整张地图(根)"] --> NW["西北"]
    R --> NE["东北"]
    R --> SW["西南"]
    R --> SE["东南"]
    NE --> A["再四分…直到叶子点足够少"]
options_en: The whole map is the root, split into four quadrants; overloaded quadrants keep splitting, and points live only in leaves.
Split by latitude first, then split by longitude.
Cut the map into a batch of fixed-size, non-overlapping grid cells.
Create one node per point and connect them by distance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把地图递归切成四个象限、超载象限继续细分,数据只存在叶子里的树结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quadtree recursively splits the map into four quadrants, subdividing overloaded areas until leaves hold few points.

optionExplanations: 整张地图就是根节点,每次超载的象限再四分成四份,数据点永远只落在叶子节点里。
先纬度二分再经度二分其实是 k-d 树的做法,quadtree 是每层同时四分两个维度,不是轮流二分。
固定大小网格不会根据数据密度调整,而 quadtree 的核心正是超载才继续细分,空旷区保持粗糙。
按距离连边描述的是图结构,quadtree 是层级分割结构,节点代表的是空间区域而不是点对点关系。
optionExplanations_en: The whole map is the root, and any overloaded quadrant keeps splitting into four until data points land only in leaves.
Splitting latitude then longitude separately is the k-d tree move; a quadtree splits both dimensions into four at once, per level.
A fixed grid doesn't adapt to density, while a quadtree's whole point is subdividing only where it's overloaded.
Connecting nodes by distance describes a graph, not a quadtree — quadtree nodes represent regions, not point-to-point links.

q: 在四叉树里做邻近搜索,候选集由什么组成?
q_en: In a quadtree proximity search, what forms the candidate set?
scenario: 四叉树里查乘客 2 公里内的司机,而最近的那个司机可能就站在 cell 边界的另一侧。
scenario_en: You are searching a quadtree for drivers within two kilometers of a rider, and the closest driver may be sitting just across a cell boundary.
options: 取回整棵树全部叶子节点里存的所有点
走到匹配叶子,加邻居叶子点,精确算距离
只取根节点里存的全部点
随机抽样出一批点做候选
why: 沿途每层和 cell 中点比南北/东西,落入匹配象限直到叶子;因为最近的点可能就在边界另一侧,所以邻居叶子也要带上,最后精确距离定胜负。
why_en: You walk down to the matching leaf, add points from neighboring leaves so boundary cases are not missed, then exact distance math picks the winners.
options_en: Fetch all the points stored in every leaf of the entire tree.
Walk to the matching leaf, add points from neighboring leaves, then compute exact distance.
Only the points stored at the root node.
A random sample of points used as candidates.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把地图递归切成四个象限、超载象限继续细分,数据只存在叶子里的树结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quadtree recursively splits the map into four quadrants, subdividing overloaded areas until leaves hold few points.

termDefinitions.meaning: 索引粗筛后留下的一小撮待精确计算的对象,不是最终答案。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A candidate set is the small group of objects an index narrows things down to before exact math finishes the job.

optionExplanations: 取回全部叶子等于放弃了索引的意义,quadtree 的价值就在于只下钻到匹配的那几个叶子。
沿途逐层比较落入哪个象限,走到匹配叶子后还要带上邻居叶子的点,因为最近点可能就在边界那一侧。
根节点通常不直接存数据点,真正的数据都下沉在叶子里,取根节点拿不到候选。
随机抽样无法保证覆盖真正邻近的点,quadtree 靠的是确定性的空间下钻,不是抽样。
optionExplanations_en: Fetching every leaf throws away the whole point of the index — quadtree's value is narrowing down to just the matching leaves.
You walk down comparing quadrants at each level, then add neighboring leaves too, since the true nearest point can sit just across a boundary.
The root node usually doesn't hold data points directly; the actual points sink down into the leaves.
Random sampling can't guarantee it catches the truly nearest points — a quadtree relies on deterministic descent, not sampling.

q: 四叉树"适应数据密度"是什么意思?
q_en: What does it mean for a quadtree to adapt to data density?
scenario: 同一棵四叉树要同时索引曼哈顿和内华达沙漠,两地的点密度差好几个数量级。
scenario_en: One quadtree has to index both Manhattan and the Nevada desert, where point density differs by orders of magnitude.
options: 缓存结构会自动压缩存进去的数据
整个结构会按访问频率自动做调整
不管数据疏密,所有区域的树深度都保持完全一致
密集区长成深子树,空旷区留粗cell
why: 分裂只发生在超载的象限:密集区自然长得深,空旷区保持粗糙。这是优点,但也埋下"深度不均"的隐患。
why_en: Dense areas like Manhattan grow deep subtrees while an empty lake stays one coarse cell, so no space is wasted subdividing emptiness.
options_en: The cache automatically compresses whatever is stored.
The structure adjusts itself based on access frequency.
Regardless of density, every region keeps exactly the same tree depth.
Dense areas grow into deep subtrees while empty areas stay one coarse cell.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把地图递归切成四个象限、超载象限继续细分,数据只存在叶子里的树结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quadtree recursively splits the map into four quadrants, subdividing overloaded areas until leaves hold few points.

optionExplanations: 这里讲的是空间索引结构,和缓存压缩数据完全是两回事,quadtree 不做数据压缩。
quadtree 按的是数据密度分裂,不是访问频率,一个冷门但密集的区域照样会分裂得很深。
如果所有区域深度一致,quadtree 就退化成固定网格了,恰恰失去了自适应密度的优点。
分裂只发生在超载的象限,曼哈顿这种密集区会长出很深的子树,空旷的湖区留一个粗粒度cell就够。
optionExplanations_en: This is a spatial index, not a cache — a quadtree doesn't compress the data it stores.
A quadtree splits based on data density, not access frequency; a cold-but-dense area still splits just as deep.
If every region kept the same depth, a quadtree would just be a fixed grid, losing exactly the density adaptivity it's known for.
Splits only happen where a quadrant is overloaded, so dense Manhattan grows deep subtrees while an empty lake stays one coarse cell.

q: 四叉树在规模上的第一个麻烦——"深度问题"是什么?
q_en: What is the quadtree "depth problem" at scale?
scenario: 四叉树索引全球司机,但 SLO 要求 p99 查询延迟可预测,而曼哈顿的簇极其密集。
scenario_en: A quadtree indexes drivers worldwide, but your SLO demands a predictable p99 latency and the Manhattan cluster is extremely dense.
options: 树的深度被写死了,不能再继续加深
按几何中点分裂,密集簇反复切,延迟因地而异
分裂做得越深,候选集越大,查询精度反而变得更低
树太深会直接导致内存发生泄漏
why: 分裂点与数据无关,曼哈顿这种密集簇要切很多刀才分得开;结果是延迟随地点漂移、最热区域最慢,worst case 很难推理。
why_en: Splits land at geometric midpoints rather than where data sits, so dense clusters need many levels and the busiest regions become the slowest to query.
options_en: The tree's depth is fixed and can never grow deeper.
Splits land at the geometric midpoint, so dense clusters get halved repeatedly and latency varies by location.
Deeper splitting yields larger candidate sets and actually makes results less precise.
Getting too deep causes an outright memory leak.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把地图递归切成四个象限、超载象限继续细分,数据只存在叶子里的树结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quadtree recursively splits the map into four quadrants, subdividing overloaded areas until leaves hold few points.

optionExplanations: quadtree 的深度是动态的,超载就继续分裂,并没有写死的深度上限。
分裂点按几何中点切,不管数据到底怎么分布,密集簇要反复对半切才分得开,查询延迟就随地点漂移。
分裂越深实际是精度越高、候选集越小,查询更准而不是更差,这个选项方向反了。
深度增加只是多几层节点,是正常的树结构增长,不会导致内存泄漏这种bug。
optionExplanations_en: A quadtree's depth is dynamic — overloaded quadrants just keep splitting; there's no hardcoded depth ceiling.
Splits land at the geometric midpoint regardless of where data clusters, so a dense area needs many halvings, and latency drifts by location.
Deeper splitting actually means tighter cells and a smaller candidate set — more precise, not less. This has it backwards.
More depth is just more tree levels, ordinary structural growth — not a memory leak bug.

q: 四叉树在规模上的第二个麻烦——"磁盘问题"是什么?
q_en: What is the quadtree "disk problem" at scale?
scenario: 四叉树要索引 5 亿个点,索引远大于 RAM,必须常驻磁盘。
scenario_en: Your quadtree must index five hundred million points, far more than fits in RAM, so it has to live on disk.
options: 四叉树整体占用的磁盘空间太大,根本存不下
四叉树的结构根本无法序列化
指针结构上磁盘后,每跳都可能是一次随机读
四叉树只能存整数类型的坐标
why: 指针结构在 RAM 里如鱼得水,上了磁盘就是灾难:每跳都可能命中未加载的页,变成随机 I/O。要上盘需要更结实的结构。
why_en: A quadtree is a pointer structure, and on disk every pointer hop risks a random page read, leaving you waiting on the disk after a few hops.
options_en: A quadtree takes up far too much disk space to store at all.
A quadtree's structure literally cannot be serialized.
It's a pointer structure, so each hop on disk risks a random read.
A quadtree can only store integer-typed coordinates.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把地图递归切成四个象限、超载象限继续细分,数据只存在叶子里的树结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quadtree recursively splits the map into four quadrants, subdividing overloaded areas until leaves hold few points.

optionExplanations: 空间占用不是核心痛点,quadtree 的节点本身很小,真正的问题出在磁盘访问模式上。
quadtree 完全可以序列化(比如写成JSON或二进制),只是读取时仍要重建指针跳转。
quadtree 靠指针从一个节点跳到下一个,一旦这些节点分散在磁盘不同页上,每跳都可能触发一次随机I/O。
quadtree 对坐标类型没有限制,浮点坐标一样能用,这不是它上磁盘困难的原因。
optionExplanations_en: Space usage isn't the real pain point — quadtree nodes are tiny; the real issue is the disk access pattern.
A quadtree can be serialized to JSON or binary fine; the problem is reading it back still means rebuilding pointer hops.
A quadtree hops from node to node via pointers, and once those nodes scatter across disk pages, each hop can trigger a random read.
Quadtrees place no restriction on coordinate type — floats work fine; that's not why disk performance suffers.

q: 四叉树今天仍活跃在哪些地方?
q_en: Where are quadtrees still useful today?
scenario: 评估四叉树今天的落点:一端是 RAM 内的实时几何计算,一端是超过 RAM 的磁盘主索引。

内存场景:地图瓦片、游戏碰撞检测
只出现在教科书的例子里
被用作分布式对象存储系统

why_en: Quadtrees remain everywhere in memory, from map tiles to game collision detection, just not as on-disk database indexes.
options_en: As the default on-disk spatial index inside mainstream databases.
In-memory use cases: map tiles, game collision detection.
Only as an example in computer science textbooks.
As the backbone of distributed object storage systems.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quadtree recursively splits the map into four quadrants, subdividing overloaded areas until leaves hold few points.

optionExplanations: 主流数据库的磁盘空间索引早就换成了 BKD 或 R-tree,quadtree 的磁盘问题没被解决,不会被选用。
quadtree 在内存里依然活跃,比如地图瓦片渲染、游戏引擎的碰撞检测,这些场景不需要它上磁盘。
它不只是教材案例,今天很多实际的内存场景仍在用,只是数据库索引这个战场让位给了别的结构。
分布式对象存储管理的是文件而不是空间坐标,和quadtree解决的邻近搜索问题不是一回事。
optionExplanations_en: Mainstream databases moved on-disk spatial indexes to BKD or R-trees long ago; quadtree's disk problem was never solved for that role.
Quadtrees stay busy in memory — map tile rendering, game engine collision detection — places that never need it on disk.
It's not just a textbook example; plenty of real in-memory workloads still use it, it just lost the on-disk database battle.
Distributed object storage manages files, not spatial coordinates — a different problem from the proximity search quadtrees solve.

q: 在"分裂方式"这个维度上,四叉树和 k-d 树的区别是?
q_en: On the split rule dimension, how do quadtrees and k-d trees differ?
scenario: 要索引的不只是经纬度,而是 6 维特征向量,分裂路数会随维度指数增长。
scenario_en: You need to index six-dimensional feature vectors, not just latitude and longitude, so the branching factor blows up with dimensionality.
options: 四叉树同时切两维,k-d 树逐层轮换切一维
两者都是四路分裂的树
k-d 树按四个维度做分裂
四叉树其实是二叉分裂,k-d 树反而是四路分裂
why: k-d 树是四叉树的二叉表亲:第一层切 x、第二层切 y、循环往复,得到多维数据的二叉树;始终按中位数切就能保持平衡。
why_en: A quadtree splits both dimensions at once into four quadrants, while a k-d tree alternates one dimension per level in a binary tree.
options_en: A quadtree splits both dimensions at once into four; a k-d tree alternates one dimension per level, splitting into two.
Both of them split four ways at every node.
A k-d tree splits across four separate dimensions.
A quadtree actually splits in two, while a k-d tree splits four ways.
tradeoff: 四叉树同时切两维、四路分裂 vs k-d 树逐层轮换切一维、二路分裂

termDefinitions.meaning: 把地图递归切成四个象限、超载象限继续细分,数据只存在叶子里的树结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quadtree recursively splits the map into four quadrants, subdividing overloaded areas until leaves hold few points.

termDefinitions.meaning: 逐层轮换按一个维度二分、用于多维最近邻搜索的二叉树。

optionExplanations: 四叉树每层同时切经纬两维、四路分裂;k-d 树每层只切一维、循环交替,是二路分裂。
只有四叉树是四路分裂,k-d 树逐层只二分一个维度,两者的分裂方式并不相同。
k-d 树的"k"指数据维度数,但每层只挑一个维度切,不是同时按四个维度分裂。
反了:四叉树是四路分裂(不是二叉),k-d 树才是逐层二分的二叉树。
optionExplanations_en: A quadtree splits both lat and lon at once into four children per level; a k-d tree alternates one dimension per level, splitting into two.
Only the quadtree is four-way; a k-d tree binary-splits one dimension per level, so the split rules differ.
The 'k' in k-d tree names how many dimensions the data has, but each level still splits on just one of them.

q: 关于 k-d 树,哪个说法正确?
q_en: Which statement about k-d trees is correct?
scenario: 内存里做 1000 万点的最近邻检索表现很好,现在要求同一个索引落盘持久化。

它只能处理二维平面的数据
它的树结构没法保持平衡

why_en: A k-d tree stays balanced by splitting at the median and served nearest-neighbor search for decades, but its pointer structure makes it painful beyond RAM.
options_en: It's naturally suited to sit directly on disk for persistence.
It can only handle two-dimensional data.
Its tree structure can never stay balanced.
Splitting at the median keeps it balanced, but it's painful once it leaves RAM.

termDefinitions.meaning: 逐层轮换按一个维度二分、用于多维最近邻搜索的二叉树。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A k-d tree is a binary tree that alternates splitting on one dimension per level for multi-dimensional nearest-neighbor search.

optionExplanations: k-d 树是纯指针结构,天生没有页对齐设计,上磁盘一样会碰到随机I/O问题,并不天生适合。

The 'k' in k-d tree stands for any number of dimensions, not just two — it handles 3D or higher nearest-neighbor search fine.

q: BKD 树(block k-d tree)对 k-d 树做了什么现代化改造?
q_en: What modernization does a BKD tree add to a k-d tree?
scenario: 要把 k-d 树的思想落到磁盘上:数据量远超 RAM,写入以批量导入为主、几乎不改。
scenario_en: You want the k-d tree idea to work on disk, where the data far exceeds RAM and writes are bulk imports that rarely change.
options: 把整棵树改造成一张哈希表
点打包进磁盘页大小的块,整树一次性批量构建
给每个节点单独加一层缓存
改用 GPU 并行地把整棵树一次性构建出来
why: BKD 用"页大小的块"解决磁盘问题,但代价是整树批量构建——本质上是 write-once,天生不爱频繁变动的数据。
why_en: A BKD tree packs points into disk-page-sized blocks and is built once from a batch, making it disk friendly but essentially write-once.
options_en: Turn the whole tree into a hash table.
Pack points into disk-page-sized blocks and build the whole tree once in a batch.
Add a separate cache layer to every node.
Rebuild the whole tree in parallel on a GPU in one pass.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: A BKD tree packs points into disk-page-sized blocks and is built once from a batch, making it disk friendly but essentially write-once.

termDefinitions.meaning: 逐层轮换按一个维度二分、用于多维最近邻搜索的二叉树。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A k-d tree is a binary tree that alternates splitting on one dimension per level for multi-dimensional nearest-neighbor search.

optionExplanations: 哈希表没有排序和范围查询能力,BKD 树要解决的恰恰是范围/邻近查询,改成哈希表方向就错了。
BKD 把点打包进磁盘页大小的块解决磁盘问题,但代价是整树要一次性批量构建,天生不爱频繁更新。
加缓存能缓解重复查询,但不解决树本身怎样在磁盘上保持磁盘友好的结构问题。

BKD packs points into disk-page-sized blocks to fix the disk problem, at the cost of building the whole tree once in a batch — essentially write-once.
A cache layer could speed up repeated queries, but it doesn't address how the tree itself stays disk-friendly.
A GPU can speed up batch computation, but BKD's real innovation is the block layout, not which hardware built it.

q: Elasticsearch 的 geo 字段今天底层用的是什么索引?

BKD 树,块结构、磁盘友好索引
倒排索引,词到文档的映射

why_en: Elasticsearch geo fields use BKD trees, the k-d tree idea repackaged into a disk-friendly block-structured index.
options_en: An R-tree, built from nested minimum bounding rectangles.
A geohash prefix tree structure.
A BKD tree — the k-d tree idea repacked as a disk-friendly block index.
An inverted index mapping terms to documents.

optionExplanations: R-tree 是另一条空间树谱系,ES 的 geo 字段走的是 k-d 树这一支的磁盘友好版本,不是 R-tree。

ES 的 geo_distance 查询底层就是 BKD 树:把点打包进磁盘页大小的块,牺牲高频更新换来磁盘友好。
倒排索引是文本搜索的核心结构,处理的是词到文档,geo 字段索引的是坐标,走的是完全不同的树。
optionExplanations_en: R-tree is a different spatial-tree lineage; ES geo fields use the disk-friendly branch of the k-d tree family instead.
Geohash is the encoded-key route, a different technology from the block-structured index ES geo fields actually use.
Elasticsearch's geo_distance query runs on a BKD tree: points packed into disk-page-sized blocks, trading update speed for disk friendliness.

q: R-tree 在空间索引史上的地位是什么?
q_en: What was the R-tree's role in spatial-index history?
scenario: 1984 年数据库要索引县界多边形和高速公路线,索引又必须住在磁盘上、边写边查。
scenario_en: In 1984 a database had to index county polygons and highway lines while keeping the index on disk and writable in place.
options: 第一个为磁盘设计,同时解决形状与磁盘问题
第一个只能活在内存里的空间索引
其实它是 geohash 的直接前身
只被用来做图形渲染,并不做索引
why: 之前的树都假设数据是点、且都是指针结构;R-tree 从数据库需求出发,同时搞定了多边形/线等形状和磁盘友好两大难题。
why_en: The R-tree was the first spatial index built from the ground up for on-disk databases, solving both the shapes problem and the disk problem.
options_en: The first index designed from scratch for disk, solving both the shape problem and the disk problem.
The first spatial index that only ever lived in memory.
It was actually the direct predecessor of geohash.
It was used only for rendering graphics, not indexing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用嵌套的最小外接矩形组织空间对象、像 B-tree 一样能在磁盘上保持平衡的索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An R-tree organizes spatial objects with nested bounding rectangles and stays balanced on disk just like a B-tree.

optionExplanations: 早期空间树只当数据是点、结构全靠指针跳转;R-tree 换了个出发点,把形状表达和磁盘友好一起做进设计里。
恰恰相反,R-tree 的历史意义正在于它是第一个为磁盘数据库设计的空间索引,不是只活在内存里。
geohash 走的是完全不同的编码键路线,和 R-tree 的矩形嵌套树结构没有继承关系。
R-tree 是数据库索引结构,渲染只是空间数据的一种应用场景,不是它被发明的目的。
optionExplanations_en: Earlier trees assumed point data and pure pointer structures; R-tree was built from database needs, solving both shapes and disk-friendliness at once.
The opposite is true — R-tree's historic significance is being the first spatial index designed for on-disk databases, not memory-only use.
Geohash follows the completely separate encoded-key route; it has no lineage connection to R-tree's nested-rectangle structure.
R-tree is a database indexing structure; rendering is just one application of spatial data, not why it was invented.

q: 为什么县界、高速公路这类几何对象放不进四叉树?
q_en: Why can't county boundaries or highways fit cleanly into a quadtree?
scenario: 现有索引是点四叉树,新需求要索引县界、高速公路和星巴克的配送区多边形。
scenario_en: Your existing index is a point quadtree, and now you must index county boundaries, highways, and Starbucks delivery polygons.
options: 它们对坐标精度的要求太高了
四叉树的实现只支持整数坐标
这些几何对象体积太大,内存里根本放不下
四叉树假设一物一坐标,县却是跨格的多边形
why: 点索引的世界观是"万物有一个坐标";而公路是线、县是多边形,连星巴克都有个多边形配送区——形状数据需要能包住形状的索引。
why_en: A county sprawls across many cells rather than sitting at one spot, so point-oriented indexes like quadtrees cannot meaningfully hold it.
options_en: Their coordinates need too much decimal precision.
A quadtree's implementation only supports integer coordinates.
These geometry objects are simply too large to fit in memory.
A quadtree assumes one coordinate per object, but a county spans many cells.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把地图递归切成四个象限、超载象限继续细分,数据只存在叶子里的树结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quadtree recursively splits the map into four quadrants, subdividing overloaded areas until leaves hold few points.

optionExplanations: 精度和这道题的核心矛盾无关,不管坐标多精确,一个多边形照样会跨越多个格子。
quadtree 对坐标类型没有限制,浮点坐标一样能用,问题不出在数字类型上。
多边形对象本身不大,真正的麻烦是它跨越多个格子后该存进哪个节点没法确定。
quadtree 默认每个对象只有一个坐标,而县界、公路这类形状会横跨很多格,压根塞不进这个假设。
optionExplanations_en: Precision isn't the real conflict here — however precise the coordinates are, a polygon still spans multiple cells.
A quadtree places no restriction on coordinate type; floats work fine, so this isn't a numeric-type issue.
The polygon object itself isn't large; the real trouble is deciding which single cell it belongs to once it spans several.
A quadtree assumes one coordinate per object, but shapes like county borders or highways sprawl across many cells, breaking that assumption.

q: R-tree 的核心构件——最小外接矩形(MBR)是怎么用的?
q_en: How does an R-tree use its core building block, the MBR?
scenario: 一棵树里要同时装点(司机)、线(道路)、多边形(配送区),索引单元必须统一成一种形状。
scenario_en: One tree has to hold points for drivers, lines for roads, and polygons for delivery zones, so the index unit must collapse to a single shape.
options: 只有多边形才用外接矩形,点和线对象都不需要
包住每个对象的最小矩形,邻近矩形再层层嵌套到根
把所有对象都裁成同样大小的矩形
矩形只用来显示,不参与索引查询
why: MBR 把任意形状统一成"矩形"这一种索引单元:先包住每个对象,再层层聚合装箱,于是点、线、多边形都能进同一棵树。
why_en: Every object gets wrapped in its minimum bounding rectangle, and nearby rectangles nest inside larger ones all the way up to the root.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A["Root MBR"] --> B["Child MBR"]
  A --> C["Child MBR"]
  B --> D["Shapes"]
  C --> E["Shapes"]
options_en: Only polygons use bounding rectangles; points and lines don't need them.
Wrap every object in its smallest bounding rectangle, then nest nearby rectangles up to the root.
Every object gets clipped down to the same fixed rectangle size.
The rectangle is only for display, not part of the index.

termDefinitions.meaning: 包住一个几何对象、边与经纬度轴平行的最小矩形。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An MBR is the smallest axis-aligned rectangle that fully contains a shape.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用嵌套的最小外接矩形组织空间对象、像 B-tree 一样能在磁盘上保持平衡的索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An R-tree organizes spatial objects with nested bounding rectangles and stays balanced on disk just like a B-tree.

optionExplanations: 点对象一样会被包进一个退化成一个点的最小矩形,MBR 是对所有几何类型统一的处理方式。
每个对象先被包进能容纳它的最小矩形,再把邻近的矩形一层层聚合装箱,直到装满到根节点。
MBR 的大小取决于对象本身,不是固定尺寸——大对象矩形大,小对象矩形小,不会被统一裁剪。
矩形正是索引查询用来粗筛的单元,查询要先判断是否与矩形相交,不是单纯用来显示。
optionExplanations_en: Point objects still get wrapped in an MBR that just degenerates to a single point — MBR is a uniform treatment across geometry types.
Each object is wrapped in the smallest rectangle that contains it, and nearby rectangles nest into larger ones up to the root.
MBR size depends on the object itself, not a fixed dimension — big objects get big boxes, small ones get small boxes.
The rectangle is exactly the coarse-filter unit a query checks for intersection against — it's not just for display.

q: R-tree 凭什么能像 B-tree 一样当数据库索引?
q_en: Why can an R-tree work as a database index like a B-tree?
scenario: PostGIS 要让空间索引像 B-tree 一样进数据库:索引大于 RAM,司机位置还在持续写入。
scenario_en: PostGIS wants a spatial index that behaves like a B-tree: bigger than RAM, with driver positions still being written constantly.
options: 它把全部空间数据都常驻在内存里避免读盘
它的索引结构从来不需要更新
叶子同深度、页大小节点,分裂合并维持平衡
它靠布隆过滤器来加速查询
why: R-tree 满足数据库索引的三件套:随数据变化保持平衡、从磁盘快速读取、司机每动一下都能便宜地更新——这正是"空间版 B-tree"的含义。
why_en: An R-tree stays balanced with all leaves at the same depth and page-sized nodes, splitting and merging pages exactly like a B-tree.
options_en: It keeps all the spatial data resident in memory to avoid disk reads.
Its index structure never needs to be updated.
Leaves stay at the same depth, and pages split or merge to stay balanced.
It relies on a Bloom filter to speed up lookups.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用嵌套的最小外接矩形组织空间对象、像 B-tree 一样能在磁盘上保持平衡的索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An R-tree organizes spatial objects with nested bounding rectangles and stays balanced on disk just like a B-tree.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种把排序键打包进磁盘页、天然保持平衡的树形索引结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree is a self-balancing tree index that packs sorted keys into disk pages for fast range scans.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种概率型的成员判断结构,可能有假阳性但不会有假阴性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Bloom filter is a probabilistic membership structure that can have false positives but never false negatives.

optionExplanations: R-tree 恰恰是为磁盘设计的,不要求数据常驻内存,这正是它能当数据库索引的原因之一。
R-tree 完全支持更新,插入删除都会触发矩形的重新计算和可能的节点分裂合并。
叶子保持同深度、节点是页大小,数据变化时靠分裂合并页来维持平衡,这套三件套和 B-tree 如出一辙。
布隆过滤器判断成员是否存在,不参与空间范围查询,和 R-tree 保持平衡的机制无关。
optionExplanations_en: R-tree is designed for disk precisely so data doesn't need to sit resident in memory — that's part of why it works as a database index.
R-tree fully supports updates; inserts and deletes trigger rectangle recalculation and possible node splits or merges.
Leaves stay at the same depth and nodes are page-sized, splitting and merging pages as data changes — the same trio B-tree relies on.
A Bloom filter checks membership, not spatial range queries — it has nothing to do with how R-tree stays balanced.

q: R-tree 最要盯着的性能陷阱是什么?
q_en: What performance trap matters most in an R-tree?
scenario: PostGIS 上 R-tree 查询延迟忽高忽低,索引的是彼此大量交叠的配送区多边形。
scenario_en: R-tree query latency on PostGIS swings unpredictably, and the indexed objects are delivery polygons that overlap heavily.
options: 矩形结构完全没办法用来包含点这类对象
不同叶子节点的深度并不一致
对象一旦插入就再也无法删除
矩形可重叠,查询要下钻多分支,拖垮性能
why: 与四叉树 cell 不同,R-tree 矩形可以重叠——重叠越多要下钻的分支越多。所以真正决定性能的是插入启发式对重叠的控制。
why_en: R-tree rectangles can overlap, and a query landing in two rectangles must descend both branches, so sloppy insertion that creates overlap drags performance down.
options_en: Bounding rectangles simply cannot contain point objects at all.
Different leaves end up at inconsistent depths.
Once inserted, an object can never be deleted.
Rectangles can overlap, forcing multiple branches to be descended and dragging performance down.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用嵌套的最小外接矩形组织空间对象、像 B-tree 一样能在磁盘上保持平衡的索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An R-tree organizes spatial objects with nested bounding rectangles and stays balanced on disk just like a B-tree.

termDefinitions.meaning: 包住一个几何对象、边与经纬度轴平行的最小矩形。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An MBR is the smallest axis-aligned rectangle that fully contains a shape.

optionExplanations: 矩形可以退化成一个点来包住点对象,这不是 R-tree 的性能陷阱所在。
R-tree 靠分裂合并维持所有叶子同深度,深度不一致不是它的性能问题。
R-tree 完全支持删除操作,删除后会触发节点的重新平衡,不存在插入后无法删除的限制。
R-tree 的盒子彼此可以覆盖同一块地方,一次查询卡在重叠区就得同时探两条路径,重叠越夸张越拖后腿。
optionExplanations_en: A rectangle can degenerate to a single point to contain point objects — that's not R-tree's performance trap.
R-tree splits and merges to keep all leaves at the same depth; uneven depth isn't its problem.
R-tree fully supports deletion, triggering rebalancing afterward — there's no rule against removing an inserted object.
Unlike quadtree cells, R-tree rectangles can overlap, so a query landing in two of them has to descend both branches — more overlap, more slowdown.

q: 实践中大家真正部署的 R-tree 变体是什么?
q_en: Which R-tree variant is commonly deployed in practice?
scenario: 要在生产上部署 R-tree 索引一批高度重叠的配送区多边形,得挑一个能压低重叠的变体。
scenario_en: You are deploying an R-tree in production over heavily overlapping delivery polygons and need the variant that keeps overlap down.
options: R*-tree,靠更聪明的插入启发式压低重叠
原始未经优化的 1984 版 R-tree
很少被提及的 R2-tree 变体
基于哈希表重写的 R-tree 版本
why: 重叠是 R-tree 的命门,而 R*-tree 的插入启发式正是为压低重叠而生,因此成为几乎所有现代 R-tree 实现的基础。
why_en: The R-star-tree refinement keeps overlap low through smarter insertion heuristics and underlies almost every modern R-tree implementation.
options_en: The R-star-tree, which lowers overlap through smarter insertion heuristics.
The original, unoptimized 1984 R-tree.
The rarely-used R2-tree variant.
A hash-table-based rewrite of the R-tree.

termDefinitions.meaning: 通过更聪明的插入启发式压低矩形重叠的 R-tree 改进版,是现代实现的基础。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An R-star-tree is an R-tree refinement that reduces rectangle overlap through smarter insertion heuristics.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用嵌套的最小外接矩形组织空间对象、像 B-tree 一样能在磁盘上保持平衡的索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An R-tree organizes spatial objects with nested bounding rectangles and stays balanced on disk just like a B-tree.

optionExplanations: 重叠正是 R-tree 的命门,R*-tree 用更聪明的插入启发式主动压低重叠,因此成了几乎所有现代实现的基础。
原始 1984 版没有针对重叠做优化,插入顺序不同重叠程度差异很大,生产系统不会直接用它。

This variant name sounds plausible but almost never shows up in real production systems — it's a distractor.
R-tree relies on nested rectangles, not hashing; rewriting it as a hash table would lose the spatial ordering range queries need.

scenario: 需求是真正的几何问题:"这个配送区多边形是否包含这个地址""这条路是否穿过这个县",数据里满是多边形和线。
scenario_en: The requirement is true geometry: "does this delivery polygon contain this address" or "does this road cross this county," with data full of polygons and lines.
q: 该用什么?

R-tree 族,如基于 GiST 的 PostGIS
对 geohash 字段做前缀范围扫描
改用 H3 六边形网格来编码位置

options_en: Call Redis's GEOADD command directly to store the points.
An R-tree-family option, like PostGIS built on GiST.

Encode positions with the H3 hexagonal grid.

q: 编码键(encoded key)路线的核心思路是什么?
q_en: What is the core idea behind the encoded-key route?
scenario: 运维不允许给数据库装任何空间扩展,只剩普通 B-tree 索引,却仍要做邻近查询。
scenario_en: Ops won't let you install any spatial extension, so all you have is a plain B-tree index, and you still owe them proximity search.
options: 为每一个城市单独建立一张表
把整张地图直接存储成一张图片
跳过自定义树,把坐标转成可排序键
把坐标加密之后再存进数据库里
why: 空间树是一大堆专用机器(索引代码、查询代码、扩展);编码键复用每个数据库都自带的普通索引,这是它流行的根本原因。
why_en: Encoded keys skip custom trees entirely by turning each location into a sortable key that any ordinary index can use.
options_en: Build a separate table for every single city.
Store the entire map as one image file.
Skip custom trees entirely — turn coordinates into a sortable key for an ordinary index.
Encrypt the coordinates before storing them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种把排序键打包进磁盘页、天然保持平衡的树形索引结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree is a self-balancing tree index that packs sorted keys into disk pages for fast range scans.

optionExplanations: 按城市分表解决的是数据分区问题,和编码键把坐标压成可排序值这件事没有关系。
存成图片丢失了坐标的可查询性,索引没法对图片像素做范围查询。
核心是不再自建专用空间树,而是把坐标转成一个普通索引就能排序的键,复用数据库现成的B-tree。
加密是为了保密,加密后的值失去了原始坐标的邻近顺序关系,反而没法做范围查询了。
optionExplanations_en: Sharding by city is a data-partitioning move, unrelated to compressing coordinates into a sortable key.
Storing the map as an image loses queryability entirely — an index can't range-query pixels.

改用 PostGIS 存每个司机的多边形
why: 司机移动=一次整数更新,候选生成=一次普通 IN 查询,全程无空间扩展——位置更新洪流下这正是想要的形状,可扩展到每秒百万级写。
why_en: Snap each driver to a small H3 cell, query the rider's cell plus surrounding rings with a plain integer IN lookup, and post-filter by exact distance.
whenOtherWins: 需求若是配送区包含、路径相交这类几何问题,编码格子无能为力,要回到 PostGIS/R-tree。
options_en: Recompute the distance to every single driver on every query.
Snap into an H3 cell, query the surrounding ring with an IN lookup, then post-filter by distance.
Maintain a separate full R-tree spatial index for every city.
Store each driver's position as a polygon in PostGIS.

optionExplanations: 对全部司机逐一算距离是O(n)的暴力扫描,在每秒百万级位置更新的规模下完全跑不动。

optionExplanations_en: Computing distance to every driver is an O(n) brute-force scan — it can't keep up at millions of updates per second.
Snap each driver into an H3 cell, run a plain IN query over the neighbor ring for candidates, then post-filter by exact distance.
R-tree's write cost comes from rebalancing rectangles, and drivers moving every few seconds overwhelm that even split by city.
PostGIS polygons are built for containment queries; drivers are moving points, not shapes, so modeling them as polygons is wasted overhead.

q: 面试里讲邻近搜索,真正拿分的是什么?
q_en: What actually earns points when explaining proximity search in an interview?
scenario: 系统设计面试被问「附近的司机怎么查」,只有 5 分钟,面试官想看的是推理深度不是词汇量。
scenario_en: In a system design interview you get five minutes on how to find nearby drivers, and the interviewer is grading reasoning depth, not vocabulary.
options: 把 H3、S2、geohash 参数全背下来
直接说一句用 Uber 的方案
讲清普通索引为何失效,再权衡说出选型
现场在白板上手写一棵四叉树
why: 很少需要靠点名 H3 vs S2 拿分;"一维排序保不住二维邻近"的成因分析+方案权衡,才是面试官判断你是否真理解问题的依据。
why_en: What lands is explaining why a plain index fails on latitude and longitude and walking the tradeoffs aloud, not naming the specific library.
options_en: Memorize every parameter of H3, S2, and geohash.
Just say you'd use whatever Uber uses.
Explain clearly why a plain index fails, then reason through the tradeoff out loud.
Hand-write a full quadtree on the whiteboard.

termDefinitions.meaning: Uber 开源的六边形网格编码系统,每个格子有 6 个大致等距的邻居,方便环形查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: H3 is Uber's hexagonal grid encoding system, where every cell has six roughly equal-distance neighbors, ideal for ring queries.

termDefinitions.meaning: Google 提出的球面网格系统,把地球包进立方体六个面再切格子,格子面积全球大致相等。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Google's S2 wraps the globe in a cube and projects onto its six faces, producing roughly equal-area cells anywhere on earth.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把经纬度逐级切成 32 份、拼成一个可排序字符串或整数的位置编码方案。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Geohash recursively divides the world into thirty-two cells per level, encoding a location as a sortable string or integer.

optionExplanations: 背参数展示的是记忆力,面试官更想看到的是你能不能推理出为什么普通索引在这里会失效。
直接报公司名字听起来像结论先行,面试官想听的是你怎么一步步权衡出这个选择,不是答案本身。
先讲清一维排序为什么保不住二维邻近性,再顺着权衡说出选型理由,这才是判断你是否真理解问题的依据。
手写完整的四叉树实现耗时又偏离重点,面试更看重权衡推理,不是代码细节的现场复现。
optionExplanations_en: Reciting parameters shows memorization; what interviewers actually want is reasoning through why a plain index fails here.
Naming a company's stack sounds like jumping to the conclusion — interviewers want to hear how you reasoned your way there.
Explain why a one-dimensional sort can't preserve two-dimensional closeness, then reason through the tradeoff — that signals real understanding.
Hand-writing a full quadtree implementation eats time and misses the point — interviews reward tradeoff reasoning, not live code recall.

scenario: 系统的核心数据是几何形状:配送区多边形、道路、行政边界,查询以"包含/相交"为主,写入频率不高。
scenario_en: The core data is geometric shapes: delivery-zone polygons, roads, and administrative boundaries; queries are mostly containment or intersection, and writes are not frequent.
q: 选型与代价是?
q_en: What is the choice and its cost?
options: 编码格子——按写入成本来算最便宜
维护一棵纯内存里的四叉树结构
对 geohash 字段做前缀范围扫描来圈出候选
空间树 PostGIS/GiST:懂形状,写更贵
why: 形状数据要的是几何语义,只有空间树给得了;为此付出空间扩展的运维和矩形重平衡的写成本是明码标价的交易。
why_en: Geometric data with containment queries calls for a spatial tree like PostGIS, paying for a spatial extension and pricier writes.
whenOtherWins: 数据若是高频移动的点,编码格子的"一次整数更新"式写入远胜矩形重平衡,应转向 geohash/S2/H3。
options_en: Encoded cells — the cheapest option by write cost.
An in-memory-only quadtree.
A prefix range scan on a geohash column to gather candidates.
A spatial tree, like PostGIS on GiST: understands shapes, but costs an extension and pricier writes.
tradeoff: 空间树:几何语义、写更贵 vs 编码键:廉价写、忽略形状

termDefinitions.meaning: Postgres 提供的通用索引框架,PostGIS 在它上面实现 R-tree 式的空间索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GiST is a generalized index framework in Postgres that PostGIS uses to implement R-tree-style spatial indexing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把经纬度逐级切成 32 份、拼成一个可排序字符串或整数的位置编码方案。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Geohash recursively divides the world into thirty-two cells per level, encoding a location as a sortable string or integer.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把地图递归切成四个象限、超载象限继续细分,数据只存在叶子里的树结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quadtree recursively splits the map into four quadrants, subdividing overloaded areas until leaves hold few points.

optionExplanations: 编码格子写入是便宜,但它只懂点位置,答不出配送区多边形是否包含某地址这类几何问题。
纯内存四叉树扛不住磁盘持久化的要求,而且同样不擅长包含/相交这类几何谓词。
geohash前缀扫描圈出的是候选点,回答不了"这条路是否穿过这个县"这种真正的几何相交判断。
包含/相交需要真正的几何语义,只有空间树给得了;代价是要装空间扩展、写入要维护矩形重平衡。
optionExplanations_en: Encoded cells are cheap to write, but they only understand point positions — they can't answer whether a polygon contains an address.
A pure in-memory quadtree can't meet disk-persistence needs, and it's equally unsuited to containment or intersection queries.
A geohash prefix scan narrows down candidate points but can't answer a real geometric question like a road crossing a county.
Containment and intersection need real geometric semantics, which only a spatial tree provides — at the cost of pricier writes.

q: 空间树路线在"写入"上的软肋具体是什么?
q_en: What exactly is the write-side weakness of the spatial-tree route?
scenario: 司机位置每秒更新一次、百万级并发写,团队却提议用 R-tree 或 BKD 树做索引。
scenario_en: Driver positions update every second at a million concurrent writes, yet the team proposes indexing them with an R-tree or a BKD tree.
options: 写入操作会把整张空间索引表直接全部锁住
R-tree 重平衡矩形,BKD 批量重建
空间树的索引结构完全不支持删除
写入必须一条一条严格串行处理
why: 这就是"司机每秒动一次"的数据不该进空间树的原因:R-tree 每次更新要维护矩形嵌套,BKD 则要整批重建。
why_en: Rebalancing R-tree rectangles is real work and the BKD variant is essentially write-once, so neither loves churning data.
options_en: Writes end up locking the entire spatial index table completely.
R-tree rebalances rectangles; BKD rebuilds in batch.
Spatial tree indexes completely lack delete support.
Writes have to be processed one at a time, strictly serial.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用嵌套的最小外接矩形组织空间对象、像 B-tree 一样能在磁盘上保持平衡的索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An R-tree organizes spatial objects with nested bounding rectangles and stays balanced on disk just like a B-tree.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把点打包进磁盘页大小的块、一次性批量构建的磁盘友好 k-d 树变体。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A BKD tree packs points into disk-page-sized blocks and is built once from a batch, making it disk friendly but essentially write-once.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个搜索引擎,geo 字段底层用 BKD 树索引位置数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Elasticsearch is a search engine whose geo fields are indexed with BKD trees.

optionExplanations: 空间树的写入代价是重新计算矩形嵌套或重建块,不等于把整张表锁死,并发写入依然可能。
R-tree每次更新要维护矩形嵌套的平衡,可能触发分裂合并;BKD树则是write-once,新数据到来要整批重建。
R-tree支持删除,删除后会触发节点重新平衡;真正的软肋在更新代价,不是完全不能删除。
写入代价高不等于必须串行处理,现代实现依然支持一定程度的并发写入,只是每次写都更贵。
optionExplanations_en: Spatial-tree write cost comes from recalculating nested rectangles or rebuilding blocks — it doesn't mean locking the whole table.
Each R-tree update has to keep the nested rectangles balanced, possibly splitting nodes; BKD is write-once, rebuilding the whole batch.
R-tree supports deletion, triggering rebalancing afterward — the real weakness is update cost, not an inability to delete.
Expensive writes don't force strict serial processing — modern implementations still allow some concurrency, each write is just pricier.

scenario: 数据几乎全是持续移动的点:司机、用户设备、实时位置;写入洪流巨大,查询是"我附近有谁";多边形运算完全不需要。
scenario_en: The data is almost all continuously moving points: drivers, user devices, and real-time locations; writes are huge, queries ask "who is near me," and polygon math is unnecessary.
q: 选型与代价是?
q_en: What is the choice and its cost?
options: 编码格子(落普通索引):写廉价,但基本只懂点
PostGIS 加 GiST 空间扩展
每个城市各建一棵内存 k-d 树
全表扫描,外面再额外套一层缓存来扛住读请求
why: 移动点要的是廉价写+快速候选生成,编码格子恰好只卖这两样;失去的多边形能力本来也用不上。
why_en: Encoded cells turn each driver move into a single integer update and scale to millions of writes per second, at the price of point-only data and ring queries.
whenOtherWins: 一旦需要"配送区是否包含该地址"这类几何判断,就必须引入空间树;两者可以并存、各管一摊。
options_en: Encoded cells on an ordinary index: cheap writes, but mostly limited to points.
PostGIS with the GiST spatial extension.
A separate in-memory k-d tree for every city.
A full table scan with a cache layered on top to absorb reads.
tradeoff: 编码键:廉价写、快速候选、只懂点 vs 空间树:几何语义、写更贵

termDefinitions.meaning: Postgres 提供的通用索引框架,PostGIS 在它上面实现 R-tree 式的空间索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GiST is a generalized index framework in Postgres that PostGIS uses to implement R-tree-style spatial indexing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 逐层轮换按一个维度二分、用于多维最近邻搜索的二叉树。

optionExplanations: 移动点要的是廉价写和快速候选生成,编码格子把每次移动变成一次整数更新,正好只卖这两样,不需要几何能力。
PostGIS的重平衡写成本正是移动点场景要避开的东西,装个空间扩展来处理纯点数据是杀鸡用牛刀。
k-d树是纯指针结构,离开内存就有磁盘问题,而且按城市各建一棵没有解决高频写入的根本代价。

PostGIS's rebalancing write cost is precisely what a moving-points workload wants to avoid — a spatial extension for point-only data is overkill.
A k-d tree is a pure pointer structure with disk problems once it leaves RAM, and one per city doesn't fix the write-volume cost.
A cache can help repeat queries, but a full scan itself only gets slower as data grows — not something that survives a write flood.

q: 补全邻近搜索的选型口诀:
q_en: Complete the proximity-search selection rule:
text: 形状用{{空间树}},移动点用{{编码 cell}},并且永远、永远{{后过滤}}。
why: 这是整篇的三句话总结:索引只交付候选集,把"查每一行"缩小成"查一小片地图",最终答案由精确距离/几何计算收尾。
why_en: Spatial trees for shapes, encoded cells for moving points, and always finish with a post-filter.

q: 把"为位置功能做索引选型"的决策链排成正确顺序:
q_en: Put the decision chain for choosing a location index in order:
steps: 对候选集做精确距离/几何计算,得到最终答案
判断数据的形状:是多边形/道路等几何体,还是高频移动的点
选路线:几何体 → 空间树(PostGIS/ES);移动点 → 编码键(geohash/S2/H3)
用索引把"查每一行"缩小成一小撮候选(前缀扫描 / IN 查询 / 矩形下钻)
why: 数据形状决定路线,路线决定候选生成方式,候选集再由精确计算收尾——面试里能把这条链讲顺,比记住任何库名都值钱。
why_en: Decide by data shape, pick tree or encoded key accordingly, generate a small candidate set, and finish with exact math.

q: 这个量级最支持下面哪条设计判断?
q_en: Which design judgment does this scale fact support?
options: 全球尺度该用 S2/H3 球面网格代替 geohash
只要把 geohash 精度多加几位字符,覆盖就够精确了
高纬度地区可以直接跳过索引,靠全表扫描兜底
这个数字只会影响地图渲染效果,不影响索引选型
why: 111 公里到 0 的收缩说明同一级 geohash 格子在赤道是胖方块、在高纬是细长条,面积不一致会让候选集在不同纬度表现完全不同。要在全球尺度保持一致,必须换成 S2/H3 这类尊重球面的编码。
why_en: Longitude spans about 111km at the equator but shrinks toward zero at the poles, so flat geohash cells get uneven — that pushes global-scale indexes toward S2 or H3.
scenario: 地图服务要在伦敦、新加坡、雷克雅未克等不同纬度的城市统一做同城 5 公里邻近召回;已知一度经度的地面距离在赤道约 111 公里,向两极收缩趋近于 0。
scenario_en: A map service must do uniform 5 km in-city recall across London, Singapore, and Reykjavik. One degree of longitude is about 111 km at the equator and shrinks toward 0 near the poles.
options_en: Switch a global-scale index to a spherical grid like S2 or H3 instead of flat geohash.
Just add a few more characters to the geohash precision and coverage is fine.
Skip indexing entirely at high latitudes and fall back to a full scan.
This number only affects map rendering, not index selection.

optionExplanations: 经度跨度从赤道111公里收缩到两极趋近于0,说明同一级geohash格子面积在不同纬度差很多,全球召回该换成面积恒定的S2/H3。
多加字符只是把格子切得更小,并不能解决网格本身在不同纬度面积不均的问题,精度和均匀性是两回事。

Adding more characters just cuts cells smaller; it doesn't fix the grid's underlying area imbalance across latitudes.
Skipping indexing gives up proximity search's scalability entirely, and high-latitude cities still have real user volume.
Longitude shrinkage directly determines how much real ground area a same-level cell covers — a core index-selection factor, not just rendering.

q: 关于各方案的 ID 位数,哪组数字正确?
q_en: Which set of ID bit widths is correct?
options: geohash 每字符是 8 bit,S2 与 H3 都用 32 位 ID
geohash 每字符只有 4 bit,S2 与 H3 的 cell ID 都用 128 位
geohash 每字符 5 bit,Redis 存 52 位,S2/H3 都是 64 位
三者其实都采用不定长的 ID 编码方式
why: 32 个格子恰是 5 bit,Redis geo 用 52 位整数存 sorted set score,S2/H3 都是 64 位层级 ID。建表该选 bigint(64 位),三种编码都装得下。
why_en: Each geohash character is five bits, Redis stores a 52-bit geohash integer, and S2 and H3 both use 64-bit cell IDs, so a 64-bit bigint column fits any of them.
scenario: 要为 geohash、S2、H3 三种编码键选数据库列类型,并确认 Redis GEO 命令内部把坐标塞进多宽的整数,这样才能定好列宽和索引类型。
scenario_en: You need to choose database column types for geohash, S2, and H3 encoded keys, and confirm how wide the integer is inside Redis GEO, so the column width and index type are right.
options_en: Geohash uses 8 bits per character; S2 and H3 both use 32-bit IDs.
Geohash uses 4 bits per character; S2 and H3 cell IDs both use 128-bit values.
Geohash uses 5 bits per character, Redis stores 52 bits, and S2/H3 both use 64-bit IDs.
All three actually use variable-length ID encodings.

错——32 个格子恰好对应 5 bit 不是 4 bit;S2/H3 用的是 64 位 ID,128 位是凭空翻倍。

q: 在"一次位置更新的成本"这个维度上,PostGIS(R-tree)与 H3-on-普通索引的对比是?
q_en: On the cost of one location update, how do PostGIS/R-tree and H3 on a normal index compare?
scenario: 百万司机每 4 秒上报一次位置,要比较 PostGIS 与 H3 加普通索引的单次更新成本。
scenario_en: A million drivers report position every four seconds, and you are comparing the per-update cost of PostGIS versus H3 on a plain index.
options: 两者的更新成本其实是完全相同的
反而是 PostGIS 那边处理一次位置更新更便宜
两者都需要做一次整体重建索引
R-tree 要重平衡矩形,H3 只改一个整数列
why: 写成本的差距是两条路线分野的核心:几何树为形状语义付出昂贵更新,编码键为廉价更新放弃形状语义。
why_en: An R-tree update may rebalance bounding rectangles while an H3 update is just a single integer change on an ordinary index.
options_en: Both approaches cost the same to update.
It's actually PostGIS that handles a single position update more cheaply.
Both require a full index rebuild on every update.
An R-tree must rebalance rectangles; H3 just changes one integer column.
tradeoff: R-tree(几何重平衡,写贵) vs H3 on B-tree(单列整数更新,写廉价)

termDefinitions.meaning: Postgres 的空间扩展,基于 GiST 提供 R-tree 式的几何索引能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PostGIS is a Postgres extension that adds R-tree-style spatial indexing on top of GiST.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用嵌套的最小外接矩形组织空间对象、像 B-tree 一样能在磁盘上保持平衡的索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An R-tree organizes spatial objects with nested bounding rectangles and stays balanced on disk just like a B-tree.

termDefinitions.meaning: Uber 开源的六边形网格编码系统,每个格子有 6 个大致等距的邻居,方便环形查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: H3 is Uber's hexagonal grid encoding system, where every cell has six roughly equal-distance neighbors, ideal for ring queries.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种把排序键打包进磁盘页、天然保持平衡的树形索引结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree is a self-balancing tree index that packs sorted keys into disk pages for fast range scans.

optionExplanations: 两者的更新成本差距正是两条路线分野的核心,并不相同——一个要重排几何结构,一个只是改数字。
反了,PostGIS靠R-tree重平衡矩形,更新成本明显高于H3只改一个整数列的方式。
整体重建是BKD这类write-once结构的特征,普通的R-tree和H3-on-B-tree都支持增量更新,不必整体重建。
R-tree每次位置变化都可能触发矩形的重新嵌套;H3把位置snap进一个cell后,更新就是普通索引上改一个整数列。
optionExplanations_en: Their update costs are exactly the divide between the two routes, not the same — one reshuffles geometry, the other just changes a number.
That's backwards — PostGIS relies on R-tree rectangle rebalancing, which costs noticeably more than a single integer update.
Full rebuilds are a BKD-style write-once trait; ordinary R-tree and H3-on-B-tree both support incremental updates.
Every position change can trigger R-tree to re-nest its rectangles; an H3 update is just changing one integer on an ordinary index.

scenario: 在游戏引擎里做实时碰撞检测:全部数据在内存,对象密度分布极不均匀,不涉及磁盘持久化。
scenario_en: You are building real-time collision detection in a game engine: all data is in memory, object density is highly uneven, and there is no disk persistence.
q: 用什么结构合适?
q_en: Which structure fits?
options: 四叉树:指针在 RAM 里很便宜,密度自适应也合适
R*-tree,还要把它落到磁盘上
geohash 编码配合 Redis 做持久化存储和跨进程共享
BKD 树,批量构建的磁盘索引
why: 四叉树的两个弱点(指针上磁盘慢、深度不均)在纯内存场景里一个不发作、一个可接受;它仍是内存空间划分的首选直觉结构。
why_en: In-memory workloads like game collision detection are where quadtrees still shine, since pointer chasing is cheap in RAM.
whenOtherWins: 索引一旦要住在磁盘上、数据大过 RAM,就得换成 BKD/R-tree 这类页结构,或干脆走编码键路线。
options_en: A quadtree: pointers are cheap in RAM, and density adaptivity fits perfectly.
An R-star-tree, which then has to be persisted to disk.
Geohash encoding paired with Redis for persistence and cross-process sharing.
A BKD tree, a batch-built disk index.
tradeoff: 内存指针结构(四叉树,查询快但怕磁盘) vs 磁盘友好结构(R*-tree/BKD,抗磁盘但更重)

termDefinitions.meaning: 把地图递归切成四个象限、超载象限继续细分,数据只存在叶子里的树结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quadtree recursively splits the map into four quadrants, subdividing overloaded areas until leaves hold few points.

termDefinitions.meaning: 通过更聪明的插入启发式压低矩形重叠的 R-tree 改进版,是现代实现的基础。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An R-star-tree is an R-tree refinement that reduces rectangle overlap through smarter insertion heuristics.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把经纬度逐级切成 32 份、拼成一个可排序字符串或整数的位置编码方案。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Geohash recursively divides the world into thirty-two cells per level, encoding a location as a sortable string or integer.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的内存型 key-value 存储,自带 geo 系列命令做地理位置索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store with built-in geo commands for location indexing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把点打包进磁盘页大小的块、一次性批量构建的磁盘友好 k-d 树变体。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A BKD tree packs points into disk-page-sized blocks and is built once from a batch, making it disk friendly but essentially write-once.

optionExplanations: 四叉树的两个弱点——指针上磁盘慢、深度不均——在纯内存场景里一个根本不发作、一个完全可接受,密度自适应正好匹配不均匀分布。
R*-tree是为磁盘友好设计的,平衡矩形和落盘的额外成本在纯内存碰撞检测场景里完全是白花的开销。
geohash配Redis是为持久化和跨进程共享设计的,游戏引擎内的实时碰撞检测不需要额外的序列化和网络往返。
BKD树是write-once的批量构建结构,碰撞检测里对象位置每帧都在变,完全不匹配这种写入模式。
optionExplanations_en: Quadtree's two weaknesses — slow pointers on disk and uneven depth — simply never trigger in a pure in-memory setting, and density adaptivity fits well.
R-star-tree is built for disk friendliness; the extra cost of rebalancing and persisting to disk is wasted overhead for in-memory collision detection.
Geohash paired with Redis is meant for persistence and cross-process sharing, which in-engine collision detection doesn't need.
BKD is a write-once, batch-built structure; collision detection has object positions changing every frame, a pattern it's not built for.

q: 为什么说"四叉树 → k-d/BKD 树 → R-tree"是一条修复链而不是三个孤立结构?
q_en: Why is "quadtree -> k-d/BKD tree -> R-tree" a repair chain instead of three isolated structures?
scenario: 面试里要用两分钟讲清空间树家族,不想让面试官觉得你在背三套互不相干的结构。
scenario_en: You have two minutes in an interview to explain the spatial tree family without sounding like you memorized three unrelated structures.
options: 三棵树其实是同一个作者发明的
每代修前代的短板:均衡→磁盘→形状与更新
三棵树其实共享同一份代码
后者只是把前一代的性能又优化了一版而已
why: 把三棵树当成递进的修复链来记:每代补上一块短板(均衡性→磁盘→形状/更新),理解了"为什么演进"自然记住"各自适合什么"。
why_en: Each tree fixes a problem the previous one could not, reading as a clean chain from quadtree intuition to disk-friendly BKD to the shape-aware balanced R-tree.
options_en: All three trees were actually invented by the same author.
Each generation fixes the last one's weak point: balance, then disk, then shape and mutability.
All three trees literally share the same codebase.
Each later tree is just a performance-tuned version of the previous one.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把地图递归切成四个象限、超载象限继续细分,数据只存在叶子里的树结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quadtree recursively splits the map into four quadrants, subdividing overloaded areas until leaves hold few points.

termDefinitions.meaning: 逐层轮换按一个维度二分、用于多维最近邻搜索的二叉树。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A k-d tree is a binary tree that alternates splitting on one dimension per level for multi-dimensional nearest-neighbor search.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把点打包进磁盘页大小的块、一次性批量构建的磁盘友好 k-d 树变体。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A BKD tree packs points into disk-page-sized blocks and is built once from a batch, making it disk friendly but essentially write-once.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用嵌套的最小外接矩形组织空间对象、像 B-tree 一样能在磁盘上保持平衡的索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An R-tree organizes spatial objects with nested bounding rectangles and stays balanced on disk just like a B-tree.

termDefinitions.meaning: 包住一个几何对象、边与经纬度轴平行的最小矩形。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An MBR is the smallest axis-aligned rectangle that fully contains a shape.

optionExplanations: 三棵树是不同时代、不同团队独立发展出来的结构,发明人是否相同和它们之间的演进逻辑没有关系。
四叉树先解决了均衡划分,k-d/BKD树接力解决磁盘友好,R-tree再补上形状语义和更新能力,每代都在修上一代的短板。
三者是完全不同的数据结构实现,节点形状、分裂规则都不一样,不存在共享代码这回事。
它们不是同一结构的调参优化,而是从根本上换了组织方式来解决前代解决不了的新问题。
optionExplanations_en: These three trees emerged independently across different eras and teams — whether the same person invented them says nothing about their logic.
Quadtree solves balanced partitioning first, k-d/BKD trees pick up disk-friendliness next, and R-tree adds shape semantics and mutability.
The three are fundamentally different data structures with different node shapes and split rules — there's no shared codebase.
They aren't tuning knobs on the same structure — each changes the underlying organization to solve what the last one couldn't.

q: 如果省略"精确距离后过滤"这一步,会出什么错?
q_en: What goes wrong if you skip exact distance post-filtering?
scenario: geohash 九宫格取回 500 个候选司机,而产品要求返回的每一个都必须在 2 公里半径内。
scenario_en: A nine-cell geohash sweep returns five hundred candidate drivers, but the product requires every returned driver to be inside the two-kilometer radius.
options: 查询延迟会因此直接变慢一倍
索引结构会因此而直接受到损坏
候选窗口内超出半径的角落点会混进结果
所有靠近格子边界的点都会被直接漏掉
why: 格子/矩形是方的、查询半径是圆的:候选窗口必然包含超半径的角落点,只有逐个算真实距离才能剔除——所以"永远后过滤"。
why_en: Skipping the post-filter leaves in corner candidates that fall inside the query ring but are actually farther than the target radius.
options_en: The query simply becomes twice as slow.
The index structure gets corrupted.
Corner points inside the candidate window but past the real radius sneak into the results.
Every point near a cell boundary simply gets missed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 索引取回候选后,再用精确距离或几何计算把窗口内但实际超出目标范围的点剔除。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A post-filter re-checks the candidates an index returns with exact math to drop ones that are inside the search window but outside the real target.

optionExplanations: 跳过后过滤反而会让查询更快,因为少算了一步距离计算,问题不在变慢而在结果不准。
后过滤只是查询阶段的一个步骤,跳过它不会碰到索引的存储结构,索引本身不会受损坏。
格子或矩形是方的,查询半径是圆的,候选窗口的四个角必然会包含超出半径的点,不后过滤就会混进结果。
边界问题指的是最近点被漏掉的风险,而跳过后过滤造成的是反方向的错误——多余的点被错误地包含进来。
optionExplanations_en: Skipping the post-filter actually makes the query faster, since one distance computation is dropped — the issue is accuracy, not slowness.
Post-filtering is just a query-time step; skipping it never touches the index's stored structure, so the index itself stays intact.
Cells or rectangles are square while the query radius is a circle, so window corners always include points beyond the radius.
The boundary problem is about missing the true nearest point; skipping the post-filter causes the opposite mistake — extra points sneak in.

q: 靠 cell ID 的什么性质能廉价地做粗粒度聚合?
q_en: Which property of the cell ID makes coarse aggregation cheap?
scenario: 司机位置以 H3 的街区级 cell 存在一个整数列上;现在要出城市级司机密度热力图,不想为粗粒度另建索引或回原始经纬度重算。
scenario_en: Driver positions live in one integer column as block-level H3 cells, and now you need a city-level density heat map without building a coarse index or recomputing from raw lat/long.
options: 对 64 位 cell ID 截断低位取父 cell 再上卷
回到每个司机的原始经纬度,按粗分辨率把整张表重新算一遍 cell
cell ID 是不透明数值,只能再单独建一套粗粒度索引
先查一张细 cell 到粗 cell 的外部映射表再聚合
why: 64 位 cell ID 是层级编码,父 cell 就是它的高位前缀——截掉低位比特即得,同一列数据零重算就能上卷到粗分辨率。代价:只能落在固定的层级边界上,给不了任意半径的自定义聚合。
why_en: A parent S2/H3 cell is the high-order prefix of the 64-bit child ID, so truncating the low bits rolls the same column up to a coarser resolution without recomputing anything.
options_en: Truncate the 64-bit cell ID's low bits to the parent cell, then roll up.
Go back to each driver's raw lat/long and recompute the whole table at the coarse resolution.
Cell IDs are opaque values, so you must build a separate coarse-resolution index.
Look up an external fine-cell-to-coarse-cell mapping table first.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一个 cell 编成的定长整数标识;在 S2/H3 里它是层级编码,高位表示粗层级、低位表示细层级。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cell ID is the fixed-width integer that labels a cell; in S2 and H3 it is hierarchical, with high bits for coarse levels and low bits for finer ones.

termDefinitions.meaning: Uber 开源的六边形网格编码系统,每个格子有 6 个大致等距的邻居,方便环形查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: H3 is Uber's hexagonal grid encoding system, where every cell has six roughly equal-distance neighbors, ideal for ring queries.

termDefinitions.meaning: Google 提出的球面网格系统,把地球包进立方体六个面再切格子,格子面积全球大致相等。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Google's S2 wraps the globe in a cube and projects onto its six faces, producing roughly equal-area cells anywhere on earth.

optionExplanations: 父 cell 已写在子 ID 的高位里,对整数做位移/掩码即得,GROUP BY 父 ID 直接出粗粒度密度,零重算。
重算能得到正确结果,但整表回到经纬度再算一遍纯属浪费,层级 ID 已经把父 cell 编在高位里了。
cell ID 不是随机不透明值,而是有层级结构的编码,截断即得父 cell,不需要另建粗粒度索引。
父子关系直接编码在比特里,截断就能拿到,不需要任何外部映射表来做细粗转换。
optionExplanations_en: The parent lives in the child ID's high bits, so a bit-shift/mask gets it and GROUP BY parent yields coarse density with zero recompute.
Recomputing gives the right answer, but scanning the whole table back to lat/long is wasted work — the parent is already in the high bits.
Cell IDs aren't random opaque values; they're hierarchical, so truncating yields the parent cell without a separate coarse index.
The parent-child relationship is encoded right in the bits, so truncation gets it — no external mapping table needed.

q: 一环候选不够时,该怎么放宽搜索?
q_en: How do you widen the search when one ring isn't enough?
scenario: 网约车调度用 H3:乘客所在 cell 加一环邻居只查到 2 个司机,产品要求至少凑够 10 个候选再返回。
scenario_en: In H3 ride-hailing dispatch, the rider's cell plus one ring of neighbors returns only two drivers, but the product wants at least ten candidates before responding.
options: 再往外扩一环,把外圈 cell 加进 IN 列表重查
把 cell 分辨率整体调粗,让每个格子装下更多司机再重查
就返回这 2 个,候选不足属于正常结果
放弃 cell 查询,改成对全城司机暴力算距离
why: H3 的 ring 查询天然可自适应扩展:先查一环,候选不够就算下一环 cell ID 追加进 IN 列表。代价:每多扩一环,候选集和要跑的精确距离后过滤都变大,延迟随之上升,所以只在不够时才扩。
why_en: H3 ring queries expand adaptively: if the first ring returns too few drivers, add the next ring's cell IDs to the IN list, at the cost of more candidates to post-filter.
options_en: Expand one more ring, adding the outer cells to the IN list and re-querying.
Coarsen the whole cell resolution so each cell holds more drivers, then re-query.
Just return the two; too few candidates is a normal result.
Drop the cell query and brute-force distance to every driver in the city.

termDefinitions.meaning: Uber 开源的六边形网格编码系统,每个格子有 6 个大致等距的邻居,方便环形查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: H3 is Uber's hexagonal grid encoding system, where every cell has six roughly equal-distance neighbors, ideal for ring queries.

termDefinitions.meaning: 以某个 cell 为中心、向外一圈圈邻居 cell 组成的集合;一环是紧邻邻居,二环再外扩一圈。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A ring is the set of neighbor cells around a center cell — the first ring is the immediate neighbors, the second ring the next layer out.

termDefinitions.meaning: 索引取回候选后,再用精确距离或几何计算把窗口内但实际超出目标范围的点剔除。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A post-filter re-checks the candidates an index returns with exact math to drop ones that are inside the search window but outside the real target.

termDefinitions.meaning: SQL 里用 WHERE col IN (...) 一次匹配一组离散值的查询,H3 邻域就写成一组 cell ID 的 IN 列表。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An IN query matches a column against a discrete list of values with WHERE col IN (...); an H3 neighborhood becomes an IN list of cell IDs.

optionExplanations: 把 k-ring 从 1 扩到 2,覆盖半径更大、候选逐层叠加,几步就能凑够 10 个,是最贴合场景的做法。
调粗分辨率确实能让格子装更多人,但那是全局改动、影响所有查询精度,不是对单次不够时的局部放宽。
在司机稀疏区强行只返回 2 个会伤用户体验,正确做法是扩环拿够候选,而不是接受不足。
回退全城暴力距离正是编码 cell 要避免的 O(n) 扫描,扩一环这种廉价手段远比它划算。
optionExplanations_en: Grow the k-ring from 1 to 2: a wider radius layers on more candidates, reaching ten in a few steps — the fit for this case.
Coarsening resolution does pack more drivers per cell, but it's a global change hurting every query's precision, not a local widening for one shortfall.
Returning just two in a sparse area hurts the rider experience; the fix is to expand a ring for enough candidates, not accept the shortfall.
Falling back to city-wide brute-force distance is the O(n) scan encoded cells exist to avoid — expanding one ring is far cheaper.
